title: JSON and fetch

notes: loadJson checks response.ok, because a missing file doesn't throw by itself.
await only works inside an async function.
One try/catch covers a missing file, broken JSON and bad data.
The status line always shows loading, loaded or a clear error.

exercises.title: Read a JSON file
exercises.prompt: patients.json sits next to this file. Write async function loadJson(url): fetch the url; if response.ok is false, throw new Error("Could not load URL (STATUS)") (for example "Could not load missing.json (404)"); otherwise return the parsed JSON. Then write async function patientNames(url) that uses loadJson and returns just the names, in order.

tests.name: patientNames()
tests.hint_if_fail: const data = await loadJson(url); return data.map((p) => p.name);

tests.name: a missing file is an error
tests.hint_if_fail: fetch doesn't throw for 404: check response.ok and throw your own Error.

hints: if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Could not load ${url} (${response.status})`);

exercises.title: Low stock from a file
exercises.prompt: Write async function lowStock(url, threshold). It loads a JSON array of { name, qty } from url and returns the names of the items whose qty is BELOW threshold, sorted A to Z. If anything goes wrong (the response isn't ok, or the JSON is broken) it returns null instead of throwing.

tests.name: failures give null
tests.hint_if_fail: Wrap it all in try/catch and return null in the catch; also return null when !response.ok.

hints: Same start as loadJson: fetch, check response.ok, response.json().
items.filter((i) => i.qty < threshold).map((i) => i.name).sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b))

quiz.q: fetch("missing.json") on a server that answers 404. What happens?
choices: It resolves to a response with ok false and status 404
quiz.why: fetch only rejects when it can't connect; check response.ok.
JSON keys must be in double quotes.

quiz.q: const data = loadStock(); where loadStock is async. What is data?
quiz.why: Async functions always return promises; use await loadStock().

quiz.q: Why set "Loading..." BEFORE the first await?
choices: So people see something is happening while the data is on its way
quiz.why: Code before the first await runs immediately.

quiz.q: You opened index.html by double-clicking it and fetch("stock.json") fails. Why?
choices: Browsers block fetch from file:// pages; serve the folder with a local web server
quiz.why: Use Archie's preview or python -m http.server.
